record.original_question: Take a three-dimensional isotropic composite built from two isotropic materials with scalar conductivities sigma and 1, and suppose the composite remains isotropic with effective conductivity sigma*(sigma) I. Which scalar functions sigma*(sigma) can occur as the effective conductivity function of such composites?

evidence.quote: Problem 3: For three-dimensional isotropic composites each having an effective conductivity σ∗I and being built from two isotropic materials having conductivities σI and I, can one characterize all possible conductivity functions σ∗(σ)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider three-dimensional periodic (or, more generally, homogenizable) two-phase composite materials in $\mathbb{R}^3$ obtained by mixing two isotropic conducting phases with scalar conductivities $\sigma>0$ and $1$, occupying measurable subsets that partition the unit cell. For any such microgeometry, the effective (homogenized) conductivity tensor $\boldsymbol{\sigma}^*$ is defined via the standard periodic homogenization of the equation $\nabla\cdot(a(x)\nabla u)=0$, where $a(x)\in\{\sigma,1\}$ is the local conductivity. Restrict attention to those microgeometries for which the resulting effective tensor is isotropic, i.e., $\boldsymbol{\sigma}^*=\sigma^*(\sigma)\,I$ for all admissible values of $\sigma>0$, with the same fixed geometry. This yields a scalar function $\sigma\mapsto\sigma^*(\sigma)$ defined on $(0,\infty)$.

Problem: Characterize completely the class of functions $\sigma^*:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ that arise in this way. That is, give necessary and sufficient conditions on a function $f(\sigma)$ for there to exist a three-dimensional two-phase isotropic composite, built from phases of conductivities $\sigma$ and $1$, whose effective conductivity equals $f(\sigma)\,I$ for every $\sigma>0$.
artifact.status_search_result: The analogous 2D problem has been substantially studied (Keller–Dykhne duality, recent universal bounds for symmetric multi-phase 2D composites), but no analogous complete characterization is available in 3D. Recent literature explicitly notes that 3D analogues remain open and that analytical solutions in 3D face major technical obstructions, so the characterization problem appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Isotropic conductivity of two-dimensional three- and four-phase symmetric composites: duality and universal bounds
status_evidence.snippet: Universal bounds and algebraic characterizations are obtained in 2D; the 3D counterpart is not addressed and is acknowledged as substantially harder.
status_evidence.claim: Characterizations of effective isotropic conductivity functions are established in 2D but not in 3D.

status_evidence.title: Reciprocal relations, bounds, and size effects (Lipton)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses bounds on effective conductivity of isotropic composites; complete characterizations in 3D are not given.
status_evidence.claim: Only bounds, not complete characterizations, are known for 3D isotropic two-phase composites.
